title: Self-Guided LLM Reasoning for Error Diagnosis in Vehicle Routing Problems
abstract: Vehicle Routing Problems (VRPs) are fundamental to many real-world applications. Recent advances in large language models (LLMs) have spurred progress in solving these NP-hard problems. However, most existing approaches assume that input instances are error-free, neglecting the presence of faults commonly encountered in real-world data. In this work, we systematically investigate the capability of LLMs to detect (and correct) errors in VRP instances, and identify key limitations, particularly in handling complex instances or errors that substantially increase the LLM's reasoning burden. To overcome these challenges, we propose a self-guided reasoning framework in which LLMs autonomously generate code that provides structured insights to aid in error diagnosis. Experiments across diverse problem settings and LLMs demonstrate that our framework significantly improves error detection performance, achieving near-perfect accuracy.

title: Inteligencia Artificial Explicable en programación competitiva: análisis comparativo de métodos de Machine Learning bajo los principios FATE
abstract: This review article analyzes the application of Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) in the context of programming education, structuring the analysis around the FATE principles (Fairness, Accountability, Transparency, Explainability). A systematic review was conducted of the scientific literature published primarily between 2020 and 2026 in databases such as Scopus, IEEE Xplore, and Scielo. Based on the findings, the review also incorporates an empirical analysis of seven comparable systems that apply ML in educational and competitive programming contexts. The analysis shows that most ML models applied to programming education prioritize predictive accuracy over transparency. A structural gap is identified: the most accurate models exhibit the lowest levels of explainability, compromising the FATE principles. The combination of Decision Trees as an intrinsically interpretable model with TreeSHAP as a post-hoc explainability technique offers the optimal balance between performance and pedagogical transparency. The integration of XAI into learning analytics is not a marginal technical improvement, but an ethical imperative to transform automated assessment systems into pedagogical allies that guarantee equity and causal feedback to students. Keywords: accuracy, decision tree, explainability, FATE, method, transparency, TreeSHAP, XAI.

title: Cytometry in R and opportunities to contribute to Bioconductor
abstract: Flow cytometry researchers have a growing collection of R and Bioconductor tools available to them. But for someone who is comfortable working with cytometry data and has little programming experience, knowing where to begin can be difficult. That is the gap the free Cytometry in R course aims to fill.

title: The Amaya Axioms: A Structural Latent-Dynamics Audit Framework for Evaluating Joint Resistance to Goodhart Optimization
abstract: This repository presents the Amaya Framework, a reproducible structural auditing suite for evaluating the internal latent-state dynamics of simulated and computational systems. The framework evaluates whether a system’s latent trajectory satisfies seven preregistered structural constraints: self-model existence, identity persistence, metacognitive error decoupling, cross-partition verifiability, perturbation propagation, bounded recursive depth, and predictive advantage over baseline forecasting models. The implementation uses ridge-regularized vector-autoregressive transition estimation, chronological train/test evaluation, singular-value diagnostics, spectral-radius analysis, and empirical perturbation-propagation testing. The repository includes a multi-target adversarial red-teaming matrix consisting of 20 base seeds across seven axiom targets, yielding 140 independent hill-climbing optimization trajectories and up to 42,000 candidate evaluations. Targeted attacks reliably spoofed Axioms 4 and 7 in isolation, demonstrating that the optimizer was mechanically capable of satisfying individual constraints. However, no trajectory satisfied all seven axioms simultaneously, yielding a joint pass rate of 0/140 under the tested attack budget and configuration. These results provide preliminary evidence for joint resistance: individual structural constraints may be manipulated in isolation, but isolated optimization did not produce full-framework compliance in the tested setting. The findings do not establish strict axiom orthogonality, universal Goodhart resistance, consciousness, agency, or phenomenal experience. The framework is released as a falsifiable research baseline requiring broader model families, stronger baselines, larger adversarial budgets, real-world time-series validation, and independent replication. Methods Summary: The audit evaluates latent trajectories using seven structural constraints: self-model existence, identity persistence, metacognitive error decoupling, cross-partition verifiability, perturbation propagation, recursive depth, and predictive advantage. Transition matrices are estimated with ridge-regularized vector-autoregressive regression using a 70/30 chronological train/test split. Perturbation propagation is measured by applying normalized perturbations to latent states and computing their amplification under the fitted transition operator across 20 propagation lags. The adversarial evaluation consists of 20 base seeds across seven axiom targets, producing 140 independent hill-climbing trajectories and up to 42,000 candidate evaluations. A structured positive control and Gaussian-noise negative control are included. Key Results: Across 140 targeted adversarial trajectories, Axioms 4 and 7 were individually spoofed in 20/20 trials each. No trajectory satisfied all seven axioms simultaneously. The joint pass rate was 0/140. The structured positive control passed all axioms, while the Gaussian-noise negative control failed identity persistence, cross-partition verifiability, perturbation propagation, and recursive depth. Interpretation Boundary: These results provide preliminary evidence for joint resistance under the tested hill-climbing adversary, seed set, optimization budget, and audit thresholds. They do not establish strict axiom orthogonality, universal Goodhart resistance, consciousness, agency, or phenomenal experience. A computational representation is not the phenomenal state it describes. Code Availability: The complete audit and adversarial-optimization code, including the seven-axiom harness, multi-target hill-climbing adversary, and reproduction routines, is included in the PDF version of this manuscript. No external repository is required to access the code.

title: Machine Unlearning: Techniques, Challenges, Evaluation, Applications, and Future Directions
abstract: Abstract—The widespread deployment of deep neural networks and foundation models has introduced acute legal, operational, and ethical challenges regarding data privacy and algorithmic accountability. Regulatory mandates, notably the European Union General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR Article 17 "Right to be Forgotten") and the California Consumer Privacy Act (CCPA), legally obligate data controllers to purge personal records upon individual request. However, physical data deletion from storage disks fails to sanitize trained models: gradient optimization permanently embeds training data signatures into overparameterized weights. While complete model retraining from scratch on retained data provides exact statistical revocation, its prohibitive computational, financial, and environmental costs render it intractable for modern architectures and streaming deletion requests. To overcome this bottleneck, Machine Unlearning has emerged as a fundamental discipline in trustworthy artificial intelligence, aiming to excise the influence of designated training subsets without compromising general model utility on retained data. This paper presents an academically rigorous, comprehensive survey of machine unlearning. We mathematically formalize the unlearning problem under Empirical Risk Minimization (ERM), classify paradigms into exact, approximate, and certified regimes, and establish an exhaustive taxonomy spanning data-partitioning (SISA), gradient inversion, influence functions, knowledge distillation, parameter-saliency pruning, certified differential perturbations, federated unlearning, and autoregressive Large Language Models (LLMs). We examine multi-dimensional evaluation suites—including membership inference attacks (MIA), loss distribution divergence, and relearning susceptibility protocols—while systematically contrasting unlearning with differential privacy and model editing. Finally, we analyze critical vulnerabilities and outline thirteen structured future research directions for verifiable unlearning systems.

title: Recent Development of Machine Learning Strategies for Restaurant Review Sentiment Classification: Challenges, Applications, and Opportunities
abstract: Online restaurant reviews have grown in number significantly providing an excellent source of customer reviews for analyzing quality of the food, services offered, ambiance of the place, pricing policy and other aspects of customers' dining experience. Hence, restaurant review sentiment classification is a good way to classify customer opinions into positive, negative and neutral sentiments automatically. This review paper gives a comprehensive overview of sentiment analysis techniques used for sentiment classification of restaurant customers' reviews. It gives an insight into the history of development of these algorithms from the feature engineering era to modern ML-based approaches. It explores different types of sentiment analysis techniques, features of restaurant reviews, application areas and challenges of using these algorithms. Comparative analysis of existing research papers on this topic helps to understand their advantages, weaknesses and further perspectives. Thus, it can be seen that while traditional methods of sentiment classification are rather computationally effective, their contextual understanding is quite low in contrast to transformer- and language models-based techniques.

title: Minimum Support Augmentation in Chordal Graphical Models
abstract: Given an observed support in a finite Cartesian table, we minimize the number of distinct new cells needed to make every maximal-clique projection of a chordal graphical model surjective. For a clique path, the missing clique configurations form a partially ordered set, and the minimum augmentation equals its width. This gives an exact algorithm by bipartite matching, as well as an equivalent lower-bound circulation formulation. In contrast, the decision problem is NP-complete on the fixed six-variable chordal graph with maximal cliques ABC, ABX, ACY, and BCZ, even when X, Y, Z are binary; the alphabets of A, B, C are allowed to grow. A partial Latin square supplies the reduction and a concrete support for which the three individual root-leaf optima are five but the global optimum is six. Integer separator multiplicities also give an exact dynamic program on any clique tree. The statistical interpretation uses the classical positive-MLE criterion for decomposable models. The explicitly stated augmentation results are complete; the general AIM marginal-cone facet question is not resolved. This AI-assisted, self-audited preprint is unrefereed and makes no claim of absolute priority.

title: CoLU: Confidence-Weighted Layerwise Unlearning for Large Language Models
abstract: Large language model (LLM) unlearning aims to forget certain information while preserving others, without retraining from scratch. SoTA methods such as NPO, SimNPO, and SatImp balance forgetting and retain through whole model fine-tuning, while FOM-UL explores selective layer updates. Prior works show that suppressing target information can damage retained knowledge. This trade-off can vary across layers even under the same unlearning loss. In this work, we propose Confidence-Weighted Layerwise Unlearning (CoLU), which combines a novel confidence-weighted forgetting and retain regularization while updating a single selected transformer layer, rather than the whole model for unlearning. To reduce CoLU compute cost, we further propose Brief Layer Screening (BLS), which uses a newly defined normalized forgetting-retention (NFR) score to first rank layers through a brief unlearning trials using a subset of forgetting dataset and fewer epochs. BLS pre-selects top-k ranked layer candidates, which will then be fully profiled using full data analysis. BLS is proven to reduce the runtime of CoLU by 60.2-79.7% with almost the same performance. On TOFU dataset, CoLU improves both forgetting and retention over NPO, SatImp, and GA-based FOM-UL in all six TOFU settings, and over SimNPO in five of the six settings. On MUSE Books and News datasets, CoLU achieves the highest retained KnowMem and the PrivLeak closest to zero among the compared SOTA unlearning methods. CoLU presents a new record performance in both unlearning and retain in most settings up to date. Moreover, across the measured settings, average CoLU GPU memory usage is 77.4% to 79.5% lower than full-model unlearning.

title: Topology-Inspired Fine-Tuning for Wind-Field Super-Resolution
abstract: Scientific super-resolution (SR) models are typically optimized with pointwise reconstruction losses, yet scientific interpretation often hinges on extrema, connected regions, and multiscale scalar structure. We characterize this tension with pretrained CNN and GAN wind-field SR models. Pointwise metrics, bottleneck persistence-diagram (PD) distance, and merge-tree (MT) distance favor the CNN, whereas order-2 Wasserstein PD distances favor the sharper GAN, so even different distances on the same topological descriptor reward different properties. Motivated by this disagreement, we fine-tune the pretrained CNN with differentiable topology-inspired auxiliary losses on scalar speed, gradient magnitude, soft high-speed level sets, and local maxima, and with fixed-pair supervision, which constrains predicted values and persistence at ground-truth persistence-pair endpoints located offline with the Topology ToolKit. A loss study of 16 fine-tuning configurations, each compared with a matched standard fine-tuning control that uses only the original reconstruction loss, on a fixed 168-field benchmark (with topology evaluated on a fixed 160 by 160 subregion of each field), shows that, among the scalar-field losses, gradient supervision provides the strongest PD improvement but does not improve mean MT distance, whereas fixed-pair supervision gives the largest and most consistent joint improvement in PD and MT distances. The final objective combines these two signals. Relative to the pretrained CNN, it lowers mean bottleneck, $W_{2,\infty}$, and $W_{2,2}$ distances by 31%, 25%, and 27% (and by 32-35% relative to the control, which on its own worsens all three), lowers all three on 150 of 168 fields, and gains 1.30 dB PSNR, about half the gain of standard fine-tuning. Mean MT distance also improves, but on only 91 of those 150 fields, indicating that PD and MT capture complementary structure.

title: Visual Sanad: Auditing Vision-Language Models for False Acceptance of Qur'anic Citations
abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) are increasingly used to interpret religious, educational, and culturally sensitive visual content, yet their reliability on citation verification remains underexplored. We introduce Visual Sanad, a controlled benchmark for testing whether VLMs falsely accept incorrect Qur'anic verse attributions when the same quote-reference pair is rendered under different visual framings. The benchmark contains 2,400 rendered images built from 100 English Qur'an verses, four factual states per verse, and six visual conditions ranging from plain text to decorative and authority-framed layouts. All quote-reference pairs were source-checked and human-audited before rendering. Across 24 full model-prompt runs, we observe a sharp capability split. Proprietary API-served VLMs range from near-perfect citation verification to moderate false acceptance, whereas recent open-weight VLMs often show weak discrimination and default to VALID on most images. De-biased prompting can reduce false acceptance, but often by shifting the decision threshold toward INVALID rather than by producing strong citation discrimination. Visual Sanad therefore exposes a culturally grounded multimodal factuality failure: fluent VLMs may treat displayed religious citations as self-authenticating unless they have strong citation-verification ability.

title: Digital Typhoon Dataset V3: Benchmarking for Multi-spectral Extension and Analyzing Systematic Bias in Intensity Regression
abstract: This paper presents the Digital Typhoon Dataset V3, a new version of the longest typhoon satellite image dataset spanning nearly 50 years, designed to benchmark machine learning models on long-term spatio-temporal data. The latest addition to Dataset V3 is multispectral satellite data, enabling multi-channel models. We investigate data-splitting strategies and present benchmarking results for the Northern and Southern Hemispheres. Experimental results show that, under the current dataset construction and experimental setting, multi-channel inputs do not clearly outperform single-channel inputs for pressure regression. Among the evaluated model architectures, image types, and spectral channels, ResNet-18, full-resolution images, and Channel 1 generally provide the best single-channel performance for pressure regression. Performance also differs between the WP and AU datasets by regression target, with lower RMSE on WP for pressure regression and on AU for wind regression. These results highlight the importance of considering dataset-specific and task-specific characteristics when interpreting benchmark performance. Additionally, we analyzed systematic bias in intensity regression, which leads to underestimation of intensity for strong typhoons. We tested imbalance-aware weighting strategies, including inverse-density weighting inspired by BalancedMSE, and showed that these approaches are not sufficient to remove the bias. The dataset is publicly available at http://agora.ex.nii.ac.jp/digital-typhoon/dataset/ and https://github.com/kitamoto-lab/digital-typhoon/.

title: THE CRITERION BOUNDARY REVERSAL PRINCIPLE (CBRP)
abstract: This paper proposes the Criterion Boundary Reversal Principle (CBRP), a candidate cross-domain paradoxical systemic principle concerning the possibility that increasing the operational intensity of a criterion can expand the effective domain captured by that criterion and, beyond a critical regime, reduce distinctions among states that were previously separable. The theory is deliberately formulated without human sensitivity as a primitive variable. Its proposed operational triad is criterion C, implementing medium M, and criterion-application intensity \lambda. A minimal model maps these variables and an input state space X to an effective threshold \theta, effective boundary B, distinguishability measure D, and output Y. The central candidate architecture is \lambda \to \theta \to B \to D \downarrow in a specified critical regime. The primary case study is the Races Classification Paradox (RCP), in which an anti-racist criterion is described as being applied so intensely that neutral racial description may be interpreted as prohibited classification. RCP is not treated as evidence of universality; it is used as the phenomenon from which a domain-neutral mechanism is abstracted and then exposed to comparative testing.The manuscript develops three analytical layers philosophical-epistemological, systemic-mechanistic, and formal-operational mathematical while preserving the same mechanism at different levels of representation. It supplies a falsifiable hypothesis architecture, scale and medium independence conditions, thirty comparative case designs, a synthetic simulation framework, competing explanations, explicit failure criteria, and a fourteen-step PEP-ESD evaluation protocol. No empirical universality is claimed. Equations are introduced only when they have an operational role, and synthetic simulation is explicitly distinguished from empirical confirmation. The resulting status of CBRP is therefore that of a proposed testable principle rather than an established universal law.

title: Cost-Aware Adaptive Self-or-Mutual Coordination in Multi-Agent Systems: A Value-Driven Framework for Selective Collaboration
abstract: Multi-agent systems can improve task performance through information exchange, distributed problem solving, mutual evaluation, and coordinated decision-making. However, collaboration is not universally beneficial. Communication, synchronization, additional computation, coordination overhead, redundant processing, and delayed decisions may consume resources without producing corresponding improvements in task outcomes. This paper proposes Cost-Aware Adaptive Self-or-Mutual Coordination (CASMC), a framework that enables multi-agent systems to adaptively switch between independent agent operation and mutual multi-agent collaboration according to the estimated value and total cost of cooperation. Unlike approaches that assume a fixed communication policy or rely primarily on communication frequency, CASMC formulates the choice between self-processing and mutual coordination as a dynamic decision problem involving task quality, uncertainty, information complementarity, resource consumption, latency, and remaining operational budgets. The framework introduces a net collaboration value function, a multidimensional coordination cost model, a cost-sensitive switching policy, and a budget-aware mechanism for selecting collaboration partners and interaction intensity. It further distinguishes the decision to initiate collaboration from the decision to continue, expand, or terminate an ongoing collaborative process. The framework is intended for heterogeneous multi-agent systems rather than being restricted to large language model agents. Its potential applications include distributed robotics, sensor networks, autonomous planning, cooperative optimization, distributed monitoring, and resource-constrained intelligent systems. The paper develops a formal problem definition, an implementable algorithm, theoretical propositions with stated assumptions, and an experimental protocol for evaluating the proposed approach. Since empirical validation has not yet been conducted in this manuscript, the expected advantages are formulated as testable hypotheses rather than established results.

title: Cognitive Value Creation Architecture (CVCA) V1.0
abstract: ognitive Value Creation Architecture (CVCA) V1.0 is a practitioner-derived human–AI operating architecture designed to convert emerging opportunities into structured decisions, governed boundaries, accountable execution, measurable value, and continuous learning. CVCA integrates Opportunity Governance, Project Decision Challenge, Boundary Management, a lightweight Execution Layer, Portfolio Control, and Human–AI Cognitive Architecture into one continuous operating cycle: Opportunity → Decision → Boundary → Execution → Value → Learning. Artificial intelligence functions as the cognitive engine of CVCA by supporting sensing, reasoning, simulation, memory, monitoring, and learning, while humans retain final decision authority, accountability, relationship judgment, ethical judgment, and economic responsibility. This White Paper presents CVCA V1.0 as a field-informed, practitioner-derived conceptual and operational architecture intended for public reference, practical application, future validation, and further research.

title: First Passage Attention
abstract: Augmenting softmax attention with forget gates typically relies on summing decay contributions along the key--query path. Because such accumulation is monotonic, these mechanisms cannot selectively erase intermediate context while preserving older, structurally relevant tokens. We propose First Passage Attention (FPA), which shifts from path summation to path extrema by lowering a key's logit proportionally to the deepest dip of a learned scalar field below that key's level over the intervening span. FPA encompasses the Forgetting Transformer (FoX) as a special case, and when the field and levels follow a shared learned walk, the alive keys with unpenalised logits naturally form a stack. We show that a constant-dimension FPA head realises any subset of keys left alive by subsequent dips, whereas softmax heads with positional biases or token-level forget gates require a head dimension linear in the number of keys. In synthetic experiments, one-layer FPA heads converge to these target sets while comparable softmax and FoX baselines fail on every seed. Scaling to a 110M-parameter language model, FPA matches FoX in perplexity and uniquely achieves perfect passkey retrieval at 8times the training length, even with its key--value cache compressed to about 25%.

title: FPG-Seg: Annotation-free Retinal Vessel Topology Segmentation
abstract: State-of-the art approaches to retinal vessel segmentation typically require extensive annotations, a highly time-consuming process, reliant on clinical expertise. We present FPG-Seg, an annotation-free pipeline for retinal vessel segmentation combining classical vesselness filtering, Bayesian deep learning and topology-aware graph reconstruction to segment retinal vessel topology without manual labels. Tested across four widely used benchmark datasets for retinal vessel segmentation, FPG-Seg attains a clDice of $0.74{-}0.78$, representing $86{-}98\%$ of the performance of an equivalent fully-supervised baseline, despite using no manual annotations for training or hyperparameter tuning. As part of this work, we also provide, to our knowledge, the first performance benchmark of an annotation-free vessel segmentation method on FIVES.

title: Stateful Testing for Deep Learning Compilers
abstract: Modern deep learning compilers compile models lazily and cache artifacts across invocations. Retained compiler state can make a later invocation incorrect even when it is correct in isolation. An analysis of 26 publicly reported issues in PyTorch, JAX, and TensorFlow shows that detecting such bugs requires sequences that first establish compiler state and then expose a failure. We present Rondo, a stateful testing method that represents each test case as a model paired with an invocation sequence. Rondo mutates invocation sequences and uses a Markov chain Monte Carlo sampler guided by compilation behavior to favor rarely observed behaviors. Its three-way differential oracle compares execution without compilation, compiled execution with compiler state reset, and compiled execution with state retained. It confirms stateful bugs by replaying the same invocation with state retained and reset while preserving inputs and program state, then shortens sequences while preserving the original bug. We evaluate Rondo on four deep learning frameworks using 24 common model architectures. Rondo detects 117 bugs, including 35 stateful bugs. We submit 39 bug reports, including 18 for stateful bugs; developers confirm 35 reports, including 16 for stateful bugs, and fix 18 bugs, including 11 stateful bugs. Rondo achieves the highest behavior coverage and compiler Python source-line coverage among the compared methods, with 99.26% alarm precision. It shortens 44 of 117 invocation sequences, reducing the lengths of these 44 sequences by 83.34% on average.

title: The Self-Improvement Problem
abstract: With the rise of large language models, agentic systems are becoming increasingly autonomous, as they write code, call tools, revise prompts, and propose modifications to their own components. This autonomy raises a fundamental question for safe self-improvement: can an automated gate like a reward model or an automated reviewer reliably decide whether a proposed update should be accepted? The difficulty is structural. The gate must be a terminating, computable procedure, while the property we ultimately care about, namely whether an update is a genuine semantic improvement, depends on potentially unbounded program behavior. We formalize this mismatch by modeling agents as programs and defining improvement in terms of a semantic score that need not be computable. We study two evaluation abstractions. The first is a certifier that approves or rejects an update. The second is a search procedure that, given access to a proposal generator, attempts to output some improving candidate if one exists. We show that, in the fully general setting, no terminating procedure can simultaneously guarantee reliability (never accepting a non-improvement) and non-conservatism (never missing an available improvement): self-referential constructions can force any such gate or searcher to fail. Randomized gates with bounded error face the same limit. We then identify a standard decidable regime used in practice (bounded evaluation and a finite proposal budget) under which exhaustive simulation yields a terminating search procedure with the desired guarantees. We also show the limit of this recovery: a chain of accepted updates can raise the bounded score in every round while the true score falls. Our results draw a boundary between unbounded, universal settings where correctness guarantees collapse and bounded settings where they can be recovered by design.

title: PriorityFEC: Deadline-Aware Streaming FEC for KV-Cache Handoff in Edge Multi-Agent Systems
abstract: Multi-agent large language model (LLM) systems are increasingly deployed at the edge to support complex tasks that require collaboration and information exchange among multiple agents. However, when task contexts are passed across agents, shared context that has already been processed by upstream agents often needs to be prefilled again, resulting in substantial redundant computation. Reusing an already prefilled key--value (KV) cache can avoid this recomputation, but requires the reusable KV state to be transferred across the network before the receiving agent can begin generation. Under strict time-to-first-token (TTFT) deadlines and unreliable edge links, delivering the complete KV cache may be infeasible, making it necessary to prioritize and protect the most valuable KV information within a limited transmission budget. This paper proposes PriorityFEC, a utility-aware KV-cache handoff scheme that jointly exploits model-side KV importance and transport-side reliability. PriorityFEC first constructs a utility-aware source stream by placing high-utility KV blocks at earlier transmission positions. It then protects the ordered stream using a feedback-adaptive Streaming Forward Erasure Correction (FEC) mechanism, which schedules repair packets according to receiver feedback before the TTFT deadline. We implement PriorityFEC on a distributed edge LLM serving prototype and evaluate it with Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct and Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct across multiple datasets. Results show that PriorityFEC achieves superior task quality over the compared transport schemes, with its advantages becoming particularly pronounced under stringent deadline constraints. These results demonstrate the importance of jointly optimizing KV-cache utility and deadline-aware transport reliability when reusable LLM state must be handed off across unreliable edge networks.

title: Clonagem de Voz por IA para o Português Brasileiro em Contexto Assistivo: Desafios Comparativos em Cinco Ferramentas de Síntese de Fala
abstract: Modelos de síntese neural de fala apresentam desempenho reduzido para o português brasileiro (PT-BR) em vozes infantis, prosódia emocional e fonemas sublexicais. Este trabalho avalia cinco ferramentas de síntese por IA em contexto assistivo, com 170 gravações como corpus controlado. Dois desafios persistiram: prosódia emocional e fonemas do PT-BR ausentes do inglês. A incorporação do dataset multilingual-phonemes-10k-alpha ao StyleTTS 2 produziu melhoria consistente na qualidade fonética regional. Os achados oferecem avaliação comparativa e evidência de estratégia de baixo custo para ampliar a cobertura fonética do PT-BR.

title: PathRounds: building cell-level reference standards with one or several pathologists from a single Claude artifact
abstract: Cell-counting models in pathology need cell-level reference data. Collecting it is slow, and a single annotation pass misses cells. We describe PathRounds, a review harness in which pathologists make one-tap decisions on pre-cut crops and fields while a detector is retrained between rounds. It is designed for one or several readers and has so far been used by one. The front end is one HTML page published as a Claude artifact. Its runtime database keeps each reader's decisions under their user id, so a colleague can join by opening a shared link, with nothing to install; the database, user id and files beside the page are behaviour observed in October 2026, not documented features. The page also runs in a browser alone or on a one-file self-hosted server for clinical images. A Python library builds each round with an explicit sampling design: stratified audits with stored inclusion probabilities (Horvitz-Thompson estimates), active learning, exhaustive fields marked blind, adjudication with the source hidden, and yes/no checks of model outputs. In an eosinophil study on public oesophageal biopsy slides, one pathologist answered 2,570 items and marked 134 fields within 24 h, in about 1.8 h of active time, while the detector was retrained four times. The median crop decision took 1.24 s. Adjudication raised the field reference by 14%, from 681 to 778 eosinophils. Gamification components are designed for a crossover trial with more pathologists. The code is open under the MIT licence.

title: A Systematic Review of Hallucination Mitigation in Large Language Models Using Retrieval-Augmented Generation
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have become widely used for question answering, education, research, summarization and information support. Despite their usefulness, LLMs may generate false, unsupported or inconsistent information, commonly described as hallucination. Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) addresses this reliability problem by retrieving relevant information from external knowledge sources and supplying it to the language model as contextual evidence before generating a response. This paper studies the role of RAG in reducing factual hallucinations through a review of existing research and a 50 question pilot comparison of responses generated with and without retrieval support. The submitted report records 49 of 50 responses as correct without RAG and all 50 as correct with RAG; it separately presents a clearly labelled illustrative distribution of 46/3/1 versus 48/2/0 for demonstrating response categories. The distinction is retained to avoid presenting illustrative values as observed experimental results. The study also examines limitations including poor retrieval, unreliable sources, incomplete context and incorrect interpretation of retrieved evidence. The paper concludes that RAG is a practical hallucination-reduction approach, but it should be combined with high-quality retrieval, evidence verification and human oversight for critical applications.

title: Adaptive Routing and Collaborative Routing Between Self-and-Other Models: A Unified Framework for State-Dependent Switching Between Autonomous and Cooperative Computation
abstract: Intelligent systems often rely on a predetermined computational pathway, a fixed routing policy, or a predefined degree of cooperation among computational components. Such designs can be inefficient when tasks vary in difficulty, uncertainty, resource requirements, and the availability of complementary information. This paper proposes a conceptual framework called Adaptive Self-and-Other Model Routing (ASOMR), which organizes computation around two complementary operational modes: adaptive self-routing and collaborative routing. The framework is based on the proposed Self-and-Other Model paradigm, in which a model-level system can operate through its own internal computational pathways or coordinate with other models, rather than being defined as a particular large language model or a conventional mixture-of-experts architecture. In the autonomous mode, the system selects, configures, and executes its own computational pathways. In the collaborative mode, it coordinates information, intermediate representations, predictions, or computational resources across multiple models. A state-dependent routing controller evaluates uncertainty, expected utility, model disagreement, computational cost, communication overhead, and resource constraints to determine whether to retain autonomous processing, initiate collaboration, or transition between the two modes. The framework also supports hybrid operation when exclusive selection between the two modes is insufficient. This paper formalizes the proposed architecture, introduces a routing objective and a state-dependent switching policy, presents a reference algorithm, and develops theoretical propositions concerning decision optimality, computational overhead, switching stability, and the limitations of cooperation. It further proposes an experimental methodology for evaluating the framework against fixed autonomous routing, fixed collaborative routing, and established adaptive routing baselines. No experimental results are claimed. evidence.title: Adaptive Routing and Collaborative Routing Between Self-and-Other Models: A Unified Framework for State-Dependent Switching Between Autonomous and Cooperative Computation
evidence.abstract: Intelligent systems often rely on a predetermined computational pathway, a fixed routing policy, or a predefined degree of cooperation among computational components. Such designs can be inefficient when tasks vary in difficulty, uncertainty, resource requirements, and the availability of complementary information. This paper proposes a conceptual framework called Adaptive Self-and-Other Model Routing (ASOMR), which organizes computation around two complementary operational modes: adaptive self-routing and collaborative routing. The framework is based on the proposed Self-and-Other Model paradigm, in which a model-level system can operate through its own internal computational pathways or coordinate with other models, rather than being defined as a particular large language model or a conventional mixture-of-experts architecture. In the autonomous mode, the system selects, configures, and executes its own computational pathways. In the collaborative mode, it coordinates information, intermediate representations, predictions, or computational resources across multiple models. A state-dependent routing controller evaluates uncertainty, expected utility, model disagreement, computational cost, communication overhead, and resource constraints to determine whether to retain autonomous processing, initiate collaboration, or transition between the two modes. The framework also supports hybrid operation when exclusive selection between the two modes is insufficient. This paper formalizes the proposed architecture, introduces a routing objective and a state-dependent switching policy, presents a reference algorithm, and develops theoretical propositions concerning decision optimality, computational overhead, switching stability, and the limitations of cooperation. It further proposes an experimental methodology for evaluating the framework against fixed autonomous routing, fixed collaborative routing, and established adaptive routing baselines. No experimental results are claimed. The principal contribution is a unified conceptual and algorithmic formulation of autonomous and collaborative routing as dynamically selectable operating modes within a higher-level Self-and-Other Model architecture.

title: Is Romanization Still a Discount? Measuring the Token Cost of Human-Romanized Hindi Across Tokenizer Generations
abstract: Many Hindi speakers type in Latin script, and prior work reports that romanization cuts token counts for Indic languages by 2 to 4 times. Those estimates come from machine transliteration and the Llama 2 tokenizer. We measure the token cost of the same 8,847 Hindi sentences in four forms: native Devanagari, human romanization from the Dakshina dataset, and two machine romanizations (IndicXlit and ITRANS). We cover 12 open tokenizers whose vocabularies were released between 2019 and 2025. Machine romanization overstates the cost of romanized Hindi: human-romanized text needs 11.5% fewer tokens than IndicXlit output on average (8.9% to 13.8% across tokenizers) and 9.4% fewer than ITRANS. The romanization discount over Devanagari depends on the tokenizer. It is 2.4x to 3.7x for the four tokenizers that fragment Devanagari most (GPT-2, cl100k_base, Llama 2 and Qwen3), but for 6 of 12, including o200k_base, Gemma 3 and Llama 4, romanized Hindi needs more tokens than Devanagari (0.54x to 0.99x). Within the Llama family the discount falls from 2.52x to 1.38x to 0.94x. Tokenizer rankings barely change between human and machine romanization (Kendall's tau = 0.94). We release our code and per-sentence counts. Code and per-sentence token counts: https://github.com/Pallavrai/romanized_discount_research

title: Artificial Intelligence Agents and Consumer Behavior: A Bibliometric Analysis of an Emerging Research Field
abstract: Recent dynamic advances in AI technologies have brought about profound transformations in the marketing paradigm and in consumer behavior and interactions. At the heart of this transformation, the relationship between AI agents and consumer behavior stands out as a timely area calling for in-depth investigation in the literature. This study constitutes a bibliometric analysis undertaken to reveal the intellectual accumulation of knowledge in this conceptual domain and to examine the evolution of the literature systematically. To this end, 438 articles indexed in the Web of Science (WoS) database between 2020 and 2026 were subjected to a comprehensive examination. The research first conducted a performance analysis to resolve the quantitative structure of the field, mapping annual publication distributions, the most prolific authors, the most highly cited studies, leading countries, and institutional collaborations. It then carried out citation, co-citation, and co-occurence analyses using science mapping techniques in order to structure the intellectual framework of the field. The findings show that the AI agent literature emerging in the context of consumer behavior is following a growth trend that is gaining momentum in both quantitative and qualitative terms. Thematically, the literature was found to concentrate on the transparency and interpretability of AI algorithms, the implications of these algorithms for consumer attitudes and behavior, the strengthening of human-AI interaction through anthropomorphic design elements, the dark side encompassing ethics, privacy, and trust, and sectoral reflections in the service industry.

title: Behavioral Organization in Embodied AI: A Three-Level Survey
abstract: Recent years have witnessed a rapid proliferation of learning, control, and planning algorithms for embodied AI. However, grouping methods by model family or learning paradigm often separates approaches serving the same behavioral function, hindering comparison. To address this gap, this survey classifies robotic manipulation research into three functional levels: sensorimotor behavior, reusable units, and task organization. This functional perspective brings together reinforcement learning approaches, vision-language-action models, world models, and code-as-policy methods. The taxonomy supports comparison within functional categories and the transfer of ideas across approaches, offering insights for future algorithm development toward more adaptable embodied systems.

title: Normalizing Flow Maps
abstract: Scalable approaches to learning neural dynamical systems have placed diffusion, flow matching, and few-step generators in flow maps at the forefront of generative modeling. Such state-of-the-art models have limited access to explicit model densities despite evolving from classical generative modeling approaches that leveraged tractable likelihoods, e.g., Normalizing Flows and Autoregressive models. In this paper, we combine these threads of few-step generation and tractable sample likelihoods and introduce Normalizing Flow Maps (NFM), a class of exactly invertible pushforward maps that generalizes normalizing flows and flow maps. More precisely, NFMs learn the integrator of an underlying dynamical system, but crucially, they provide efficient exact likelihood evaluation by construction. To enable scalable training of NFMs, we derive two complementary axes of consistency inherent to NFMs that yield (self) distillation objectives: (1) pointwise matching, which unlocks ell_2-based flow-map style regression losses, and (2) distributional matching, which matches pushforward distributions to the marginals of a prescribed forward process. On conditional image generation on CIFAR-10 and ImageNet-64, NFMs achieve state-of-the-art sample quality among parameter-matched normalizing flows, while supporting likelihood-based RLHF. For equilibrium sampling in Boltzmann Generators, NFMs outperform prior state-of-the-art normalizing flows on both single-system and transferable peptide benchmarks.

title: Denoising Textures is a Different Ballgame Altogether!
abstract: The human brain effortlessly deciphers colors and textures from visual stimuli and reconstructs the world around us, yet preserving such details remains challenging in image denoising. While significant progress has been made in generic image denoising, the problem of texture denoising has remained relatively under-explored. Fine details, such as intricate patterns and repetitive structures, often suffer from over-smoothing even in deep learning based approaches for denoising. In this paper, we analyze the behavior of state-of-the-art (SOTA) denoisers on texture datasets and show that performance improvements are possible only by fine-tuning the denoisers on the texture datasets. Surprisingly, fine-tuning on texture datasets result in the models catastrophically forgetting the original dataset. These findings highlight the need for specialized treatment of textures in denoising. Since denoising quality directly impacts downstream tasks such as generative modelling, we argue that dedicated texture aware denoisers are essential for faithful texture reconstruction and synthesis.

title: Interfaces and Modules: A Scalable Representation for Weight-Space Learning across Architectures
abstract: Weight-space learning across architectures requires representations that respect parameter symmetries and scale to large networks. Existing equivariant tensor encoders require architecture-specific symmetry specifications, while neuron graphs make global attention costly. We introduce a typed graph organized around shared coordinate-permutation actions. Its nodes, called interfaces, represent coordinate spaces whose bound tensor axes must be permuted jointly; operation occurrences, called modules, form typed hyperedges. A compiler derives this graph from supported PyTorch models, with exact recovery of the permutation factors defined by its constraints. The Universal Weight Encoder (UWE) combines local equivariant updates to parameter features with global attention over invariant interface summaries. The small number of interfaces makes global attention practical, and a single encoder processes different supported architectures. UWE is competitive with architecture-specific state-of-the-art methods on established benchmarks. On a new zoo of 1,200 transformers spanning 100 architectures, it outperforms the evaluated baselines at ranking networks within unseen architectures, including architectures larger than those used for training, while using substantially less memory.

title: Calibration Language Shapes Block-Influence Pruning in Multilingual Language Models
abstract: Block Influence (BI) ranks Transformer blocks for depth pruning from their input-output cosine change, but the ranking depends on the calibration distribution. We study whether English calibration transfers to Indian languages in Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct, Llama-3.2-1B, and Gemma-2-2B. English, Hindi, Marathi, and Tamil use disjoint Wikipedia articles for calibration and evaluation; every selector receives the same 150-chunk budget, and Tamil is excluded from multilingual aggregation to test cross-script transfer. Across all three models, late-block BI is 20.7-55.5% higher for the three Indian languages than for English, and every predeclared late-minus-middle contrast has a 95% bootstrap interval above zero. This mismatch changes the low-BI blocks selected for removal despite high global rank correlations. Averaging BI over equal English, Hindi, and Marathi budgets mitigates the resulting perplexity damage for Qwen at six removed blocks and for Gemma at all tested depths, including held-out Tamil. The mitigation is not universal: on Llama, balancing improves Hindi and Marathi at two removed blocks but severely harms Tamil, while larger pruning budgets select the same blocks and collapse perplexity regardless of calibration. Rank-mean and minimax-rank aggregators do not dominate the raw mean. These results support a diagnostic claim rather than a universal pruning rule: English-only BI systematically misses late-layer activity for Indian-language text, but multilingual calibration must still be validated per architecture and pruning budget.

title: Language Models Share a Readout Bottleneck in Working Memory
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) reproduce a human working-memory signature on the N-back task: performance declines as memory load N increases, and errors concentrate on lures, items that repeat the current stimulus at a neighboring but incorrect serial position. We ask whether this shared behavioral signature reflects a shared mechanism. The literature offers two candidate accounts. On a precision account, softmax attention cannot concentrate its weight on the item N positions back, so adjacent items are retrieved instead. On an interference account, attention selects the correct item, but the content of competing items corrupts the decision. We dissociate these accounts in 15 pretrained LLMs from three families (70 million to 14 billion parameters) and in minimal transformers trained from scratch. In all three families, the attention heads that carry the task attend to the target on most missed matches. Linear probes decode near-perfectly whether a matching letter occurred at the target or at a lure position, even on trials where the model false-alarms to the lure, although its own decisions barely distinguish the two. Sharpening attention yields negligible gains, whereas suppressing the letter identity of non-target items improves sensitivity (d') in nearly all model-by-load conditions. In larger models the task is spread over more heads, and removing interference helps more. In minimal transformers, precision limits a single attention layer, but a second layer removes this constraint. The working-memory limit of LLMs therefore lies in reading items out under interference rather than in locating them, consistent with interference accounts of human working memory.

title: Joint-240 SBS Disagreement and One-Step Counterfactual Action Outcomes
abstract: Historical exploratory synthetic-simulator dataset from 240 independently seeded Joint-240 scenarios. The release contains 8,886 retained SBS-disagreement state-context records and 21,854 alternative-action terminal outcomes from 236 represented scenarios. Each alternative action is followed by fixed SBS continuation. The release preserves positive, negative, and null effects (2,573 / 3,624 / 15,657 ANWG classes at the original 1e-12 threshold), excludes 98 unresolved historical-overlap keys, and excludes already-public reference utilities and learnability aggregates. This dataset is not the Performance Evaluation manuscript's production-derived confirmatory evidence (PEVA-D-26-00474). It is historical exploratory simulator evidence used to motivate a fixed SBS reference. Canonical source: GitHub v1.0.0 directory. Data license: CC BY 4.0. title: Quantum-Enhanced Neural Networks for Cancer Detection Using Gene Expression Data
abstract: Accurate discrimination between benign and malignant tumours from molecular data is one of the most consequential tasks in clinical oncology, yet gene-expression profiles are extremely high-dimensional and challenge conventional classifiers with overfitting and heavy parameter budgets. This paper presents OncoVQC, a hybrid quantum-classical framework for cancer-malignancy classification from integrated gene-expression and clinical features. A disciplined classical pipeline of mutual-information feature selection, principal component analysis, and angle normalisation reduces fifty-eight raw features to six encoding angles, which are processed by a six-qubit Variational Quantum Classifier (VQC) employing genuine data re-uploading and a hardware-efficient entangling ansatz across four layers. The model is trained with the gradient-free COBYLA optimiser against a binary cross-entropy objective and is delivered behind a FastAPI prediction service with a React dashboard for real-time inference. On a balanced multi-cancer cohort of 5,200 samples spanning four tumour types, OncoVQC achieves 88.5% test accuracy and a ROC-AUC of 0.960 using only forty-eight trainable parameters two to four orders of magnitude fewer than competitive classical ensembles while an ablation study confirms that data re-uploading and entanglement are the decisive contributors to its performance.

title: Evidence-Carrying AI-Assisted Cryptanalysis for Post-Quantum Forensic Assurance
abstract: —Artificial intelligence (AI) systems are increasingly being used to generate and investigate cryptanalytic hypotheses. Recent reports describe AI-assisted analysis of the HAWK signature scheme, executable-game attacks on lesser-studied constructions, and machine-learning attacks against cryptographic implementations. Such results vary in logical form, attack scope, evidentiary support, and reproducibility. This paper proposes ECA-PQFA, a conceptual evidence-carrying framework for recording, evaluating, and preserving AI-assisted cryptanalytic claims for post-quantum risk assessment and digital-forensic workflows. The framework separates claim form, target scope, provenance, and assurance level; maps each claim form to an appropriate verification procedure; defines independence requirements for reproduction; and proposes an append-only, Merkle-based provenance log with algorithm-agile signatures. A cryptographic-estate model links claims to retrospective and prospective harvest-now-decrypt-later (HNDL) exposure and to migration decisions. The paper also specifies a pre-registerable evaluation protocol, a proposed benchmark, comparison conditions, metrics, and falsification criteria. The framework and evaluation protocol are conceptual: no reference implementation, software validation, or empirical study of real cryptanalytic claims is reported in this paper. The contribution is therefore a research design intended to support future implementation and evaluation, not evidence that the proposed framework is already effective.

title: Learning yesterday's news, and each user, overnight: sealed tests of continual learning
abstract: Language models stop learning the day their training ends. This report tests whether a model can learn a day of real news overnight and answer questions about it the next morning, written by a different model, with nothing added to the prompt. Every setting and the scores to beat were written down before the day's news existed. On Qwen2.5-7B, standard fine-tuning on the day's articles took the model from 7.9% to 13 to 16% of next-morning questions. Writing the day's facts into the prompt reached 76.7%. Fintan's overnight learning reached 91.4% on the same model, and 90 to 94% across four model families (Qwen, Llama, Gemma, Mistral). A 72B model reached 95.0% on 80 of the questions. The same overnight learning also learns individual users: 87.5% of facts about a person, asked later in other words, against 82.9% with the facts in the prompt. In vLLM it served 256 different people at once at 98% of the engine's normal speed, where a standard adapter per user ran at 10%. The news test's questions, facts, sources and answers are public: https://huggingface.co/datasets/fintanlabs/sealed-news-2026-10-13. More results: https://fintanlabs.com. The method itself is not described.

title: Hierarchical Multiple-Instance Learning for Vehicle-Level Battery Anomaly Detection from Charging Data Streams
abstract: Vehicle-level battery labels paired with many charging records create a weakly supervised rare-event problem. We evaluated a two-level multiple-instance framework on 191 vehicles (184 normal and seven source-coded abnormal) from the public EVBattery archive, using 38,200 charging snippets. Nine normal-reference anomaly detectors were combined with fixed or learned vehicle-level pooling under six repetitions of five-fold vehicle-disjoint internal cross-validation. All preprocessing and detector fitting used training vehicles only; score mapping used aggregation-training vehicles; decision thresholds used a separate 13-14-vehicle validation partition containing only one or two abnormal vehicles. PCA reconstruction with 95th-percentile pooling produced the highest numerical repeat-mean average precision (0.342) among 46 evaluated pipelines. A leave-one-repeat-out selection-sensitivity diagnostic selected this pipeline in five of six analyses and yielded mean held-repeat average precision 0.318 ± 0.078; because all repeats reuse the same 191 vehicles, this is not an independent test estimate. After averaging six out-of-fold probabilities per vehicle, average precision was 0.371 and AUROC 0.796. Threshold-based metrics are exploratory: the 30 validation-derived thresholds ranged from 0.267 to 0.999, and 17 equalled 0.500. No pairwise comparison survived Holm correction, uncertainty was wide, and calibration was poor. The results identify PCA plus upper-tail pooling only as the highest numerical internal benchmark in this cohort, not as an unbiased estimate of a selected final model, confirmed physical diagnosis, or deployment-ready probability estimation.

title: GlobeBench: Evaluating Text-Based World Model Capabilities for Scalable Environment Simulations
abstract: Text-based world models have recently shown potential to simulate complex RL environment state transitions for a diverse set of use cases. However, no standardized benchmark exists to compare, study and improve these models. Through this paper, we attempt to solve this problem by building GlobeBench, a novel benchmark with 1,632 tasks across five separate domains and nineteen simulation skills. The tasks check whether models can predict the environment's response to a specific action given the full agent trajectory by understanding earlier state changes, following environment rules, and predicting the effects of actions on both related and unrelated objects. We compare the predicted environment response with an execution-derived reference, using a hybrid architecture with both deterministic gates and a semantic judge. Among 20 general-purpose LLMs and specialized text world models, GPT-6 Astra achieves the highest task success rate at 49.57%. We find that model accuracy decreases as actions affect a larger portion of the environment. Specifically, when the agent's changes must propagate to dependent objects, task success drops to an average of 5.1% across all 20 models. Although model strengths differ across tasks, 631 tasks remain unsolved by any model, suggesting a significant gap in general LLM capabilities as a world model.

title: BitSparse: Compact Activation Storage for ReLU Feed-Forward Networks
abstract: Reducing memory use in large language model (LLM) training is an ongoing challenge. Activation checkpointing saves memory by recomputation, while lossy compression changes the stored activations. The reemergence of sparse $\relu$ and $\relu^2$ activations creates a third opportunity: losslessly compressing the activation cache itself. We present BitSparse, a GPU-resident lossless compression format for sparse activations. Compression and reconstruction run in custom Triton kernels fused into an autograd function, shrinking the activation cache while recovering it exactly for the backward pass. Bfloat16 (BF16) and FP8 activations are supported. Optional sign-bit packing further increases compression up to close to the theoretical limit. We analyze its compression ratio and compare it to the theoretical optimum. BitSparse lowers per-token VRAM by 31\% and 30\% Modded-NanoGPT and Nemotron-H respectively, with overheads of no more than 1\% at practical sequence lengths. Additionally, a new preallocated buffer system avoids host synchronization during training when variable size tensors are allocated.

title: Data-Efficient ConvNeXt Pretraining for High-Resolution Sentinel-1 GRD SAR Representation Learning
abstract: Labeled Sentinel-1 Ground Range Detected (S1GRD) datasets remain scarce, limiting supervised deep learning for land-surface remote sensing, while self-supervised pretraining for this domain has been dominated by Vision Transformer (ViT)-based masked image modeling requiring substantial data and compute. We propose SparK-SAR, a sparse convolutional masked pretraining framework built on SparK and ConvNeXt, designed to exploit convolutional inductive biases for S1GRD imagery under constrained compute. SparK-SAR makes three core technical contributions: (i) ConvNeXt-RS, a domain-adapted encoder that halves the stem stride (4x to 2x) to produce 14x14 feature maps at stride 16x, providing 4x more spatial tokens at identical parameter count; (ii) a lightweight ConvNeXt-512 reconstruction decoder with PixelShuffle upsampling that reduces pretraining VRAM by 7.5-8.5% per GPU relative to a UNet-128 baseline while matching its accuracy; and (iii) an empirical characterization of FP16 mixed-precision pretraining instability in the standard SparK UNet-768 decoder on S1GRD data, complemented by a finding that finetuning with layer-wise learning rate decay (LLRD) improves downstream performance of pretrained encoders. On four Copernicus-Bench S1GRD tasks, our finetuned 27.8M-parameter ConvNeXt-RS encoder improves over a non-pretrained baseline by +4.7, +5.0, +5.8, and +1.4 pp on EuroSAT-S1, BigEarthNet-S1, DFC2020-S1, and Flood-S1 respectively, and outperforms the Copernicus-FM ViT (139M parameters, frozen) on three of four tasks at roughly 5x fewer parameters. A pretraining data-scaling study reveals task-dependent data efficiency: classification saturates with as little as 10-25% of the SSL4EO-S12 v1.1 corpus, while dense prediction continues to improve significantly up to 25-50%. The study also includes a CKA representation analysis and a geographic de-collision experiment.

title: ZZ-Free bSWAP Gates under Strong Driving in Far-Detuned Fixed-Frequency Transmons
abstract: Far-detuned frequency allocations in fixed-frequency superconducting processors mitigate spectral crowding but constrain cross-resonance interactions at practical drive amplitudes. Here, we demonstrate that a single strong drive induces a large $XX-YY$ interaction in the far-detuned regime, while a weak second tone tunes the accompanying $ZZ$ phase. The interaction realizes a 150-ns $\sqrt{\mathrm{bSWAP}}$ gate, which can directly prepare a maximally entangled state from the ground state. For the implementations on the same qubit pair at matched drive strengths, cross resonance gives a shorter CNOT operation, while $\sqrt{\mathrm{bSWAP}}$ gives a 33% shorter SWAP operation with a higher IRB fidelity. The multilevel theory further predicts a regime where stronger driving can yield a speed advantage for CNOT as well, a possibility absent in the two-level model. As an application of the $XX-YY$ interaction, we also demonstrate two-spin squeezing beyond the standard quantum limit through two-axis countertwisting. The interaction realized here complements cross resonance and offers a route to efficient gate synthesis and quantum simulation of interacting spin systems.

title: MetaShare: Failure-Aware Collective Self-Improvement for Open-Ended Agents
abstract: Humans often learn fastest not by repeating success, but by remembering which failures not to repeat. Open-ended self-improving agents can share experience across lineages, as in GEA, or edit their own improvement mechanisms, as in DGM-Hyperagents, yet failed improvement attempts are rarely retained as reusable cross-branch knowledge, and search can collapse onto redundant strategies. We introduce MetaShare, a failure-aware framework that records successful and unsuccessful agent modifications together with signed performance deltas. Before each generation, MetaShare retrieves diverse high-performing strategies alongside high-confidence failures from other lineages, letting agents reuse effective mechanisms while avoiding known dead ends. A task-blind auditor periodically injects absent or underrepresented mechanism categories, while embedding-based de-ranking limits redundancy during retrieval. Multiple meta-agents propose modifications in parallel at heterogeneous temperatures behind a deterministic selector that gates applicability, scope, compilability, and size. Experiments across paper review, coding, math grading, robotics reward design, and financial audit-risk assessment show that MetaShare's median matches or exceeds DGM-Hyperagents' final performance and reaches its own best-performing agent in 1.7--2.9$\times$ fewer evolution iterations.

title: SCMerge: Spatial-Consistency-Aware Token Pair Merging for Efficient Semantic Segmentation
abstract: Vision Transformer architectures have showcased impressive performance on semantic segmentation, yet their quadratic attention complexity hinders practical applications. Recent works have focused on merging tokens to reduce sequence length and thus improve transformer efficiency. However, existing token merging methods primarily rely on feature similarity to identify similar tokens, overlooking spatial consistency, which may introduce segmentation errors in semantic segmentation. In this work, we propose SCMerge, a training-free token merging method that jointly considers feature similarity and spatial consistency in pairing similar tokens. The pairwise tokens are then merged within the encoder, and the resulting token sequences are reconstructed onto the original patch grid after decoding. The proposed method is flexible and can be plugged into existing vision Transformer-based semantic segmentation pipelines. Extensive experiments on the benchmark datasets ADE20K, Pascal Context, and Cityscapes show that SCMerge consistently achieves a better trade-off between segmentation accuracy and efficiency than baseline methods.

title: RDL-Bench: A Benchmark for Task-Aware Question Answering over Relational Databases
abstract: Relational databases (RDBs) remain the primary infrastructure for storing and managing structured data across enterprise and scientific domains. Natural-language (NL) interfaces to RDBs aim to let users ask questions without writing SQL, but real user needs go beyond SQL-style lookup: some questions require reasoning over the observable database state, while others require predictive inference from historical relational records under temporal constraints. Existing benchmarks address these goals in isolation. To address this gap, we introduce RDL-Bench, a benchmark for task-aware question answering (QA) over real RDBs. RDL-Bench organizes diverse user questions into reasoning-oriented questions, whose answers are determined by the current database state, and prediction-oriented questions, whose answers depend on future outcomes under temporal constraints. Each instance contains an NL question, task metadata, schema information, temporal context, either executable evidence or target-construction logic, and denotation-level ground truth. RDL-Bench supports two evaluation settings: native solvers under their intended capabilities, and task-aware modular systems where a router dispatches each question to an appropriate execution module.

title: Microbiome-Augmented Quantum AI for Ultra-Early Cancer Risk Prediction
abstract: This undergraduate graduation project report presents a hybrid classical–quantum machine learning framework for colorectal cancer-related prediction tasks. It investigates microbiome data, NHANES clinical records, and Kvasir endoscopic images using modality-specific preprocessing and classical, quantum, and hybrid models. The report describes model development and evaluation, together with a prototype decision-support application for doctors, patients, and administrators. The work is exploratory and does not establish clinical validity or demonstrate prediction years before symptom onset.

title: MILLIY-MADANIY VA PRAGMATIK TEGLARNING KORPUS QIDIRUVIDAGI AMALIY AHAMIYATI
abstract: Annotatsiya. Ushbu tadqiqot ishida korpus qidiruvida milliy-madaniy va pragmatik teglarning amaliy ahamiyati tahlil qilinadi. Bunday teglar madaniy birliklar, nutq aktlari va pragmatik vazifalarni belgilash orqali qidiruv imkoniyatlarini kengaytirishi, qiyosiy tahlilni chuqurlashtirishi hamda til resurslaridan samarali foydalanishga xizmat qilishi asoslanadi. Kalit so‘zlar: korpus lingvistikasi, milliy-madaniy teg, pragmatik teg, korpus qidiruvi, annotatsiya, pragmatik ma’no, madaniy birlik. Аннотация. В данной исследовательской работе анализируется практическое значение национально-культурных и прагматических тегов в корпусном поиске. Она основана на том, что такие теги, идентифицируя культурные единицы, речевые акты и прагматические задачи, расширяют возможности поиска, углубляют сравнительный анализ и способствуют эффективному использованию языковых ресурсов. Ключевые слова: корпусная лингвистика, национально-культурный тег, прагматический тег, корпусный поиск, аннотация, прагматическое значение, культурная единица. Abstract. This research paper analyzes the practical significance of national-cultural and pragmatic tags in corpus search. It is based on the fact that such tags, by identifying cultural units, speech acts and pragmatic tasks, expand search capabilities, deepen comparative analysis and contribute to the effective use of language resources. Keywords: corpus linguistics, national-cultural tag, pragmatic tag, corpus search, annotation, pragmatic meaning, cultural unit.

title: Adaptive Self-Play and Multi-Model Game Switching in Self–Mutual World Models: A Unified Framework for Autonomous Strategic Learning
abstract: World models enable artificial systems to represent environmental dynamics, predict future states, and evaluate potential actions before interacting with the real environment. However, strategic learning within a world model can be organized in different ways. A system may improve its behavior through self-play, in which a model interacts with its own alternative states, policies, or historical versions, or through multi-model games, in which multiple distinct models interact, challenge predictions, evaluate strategies, or pursue complementary objectives. Permanently relying on either mode may impose limitations on exploration diversity, computational efficiency, strategic robustness, and adaptation to changing environmental conditions. This paper proposes an Adaptive Self-Play and Multi-Model Game Switching framework for Self–Mutual World Models (ASMG-SMWM). The framework integrates a Self-Model, a Mutual-Model, and a World Model into a unified architecture that adaptively selects between self-play and multi-model game interaction according to prediction uncertainty, model disagreement, strategic novelty, expected learning value, computational cost, and environmental change. Self-play supports internally generated strategic exploration, counterfactual evaluation, and model-specific improvement. Multi-model games introduce interactions among distinct models, enabling alternative predictions, competitive strategies, cooperative planning, and cross-model evaluation. A switching controller determines when to continue self-play, initiate multi-model interaction, alternate between the two, or combine them within a coordinated learning cycle. The framework is designed for model-based systems rather than requiring large language models, natural-language agents, or a fixed multi-agent architecture. It formalizes the model organization, switching objective, game interaction, learning procedure, and evaluation protocol. The paper establishes research propositions and testable hypotheses rather than claiming experimentally demonstrated improvements. Its central contribution is the formulation of adaptive strategic interaction as a control problem within a self–mutual world-model architecture, providing a foundation for investigating when independent strategic development and cross-model interaction should be used.

title: la Descripción para Zenodo, las Palabras clave
abstract: Este documento presenta una solución completa al problema del aprendizaje continuo en inteligencia artificial, eliminando el olvido catastrófico, las alucinaciones estadísticas y la ineficiencia energética mediante una arquitectura basada en cadenas discretas independientes, indexación local estricta y números enteros puros. El sistema organiza el conocimiento en rutas aisladas que crecen de forma aditiva, garantizando que ninguna tarea nueva degrade o sobrescriba información previa. La lógica discreta reemplaza el punto flotante, permitiendo comparaciones exactas, saltos de punteros nativos y un funcionamiento determinista sin aproximaciones probabilísticas. El paper incluye el código completo del Motor Evolutivo Discreto, demostrando fases de combinación, búsqueda asociativa, mutación dirigida, creatividad relacional explicable y selección autónoma por eficiencia lógica. Se muestran resultados empíricos que evidencian inmunidad total al olvido catastrófico, activación determinista, creatividad estructural sin duplicación, poda automática de redundancias y eficiencia energética extrema. La arquitectura propuesta constituye un cambio de paradigma frente a los modelos estadísticos tradicionales, ofreciendo una alternativa basada en estructuras discretas, enrutamiento exacto, memoria inmutable y evolución aditiva, capaz de resolver el aprendizaje continuo sin reentrenamiento, sin matrices de pesos y sin riesgo de alucinaciones.

El sistema organiza el conocimiento en rutas aisladas que crecen de forma aditiva, garantizando que ninguna tarea nueva degrade o sobrescriba información previa. La lógica discreta reemplaza el punto flotante, permitiendo comparaciones exactas, saltos de punteros nativos y un funcionamiento determinista sin aproximaciones probabilísticas. El paper incluye el código completo del Motor Evolutivo Discreto, demostrando fases de combinación, búsqueda asociativa, mutación dirigida, creatividad relacional explicable y selección autónoma por eficiencia lógica. Se muestran resultados empíricos que evidencian inmunidad total al olvido catastrófico, activación determinista, creatividad estructural sin duplicación, poda automática de redundancias y eficiencia energética extrema. La arquitectura propuesta constituye un cambio de paradigma frente a los modelos estadísticos tradicionales, ofreciendo una alternativa basada en estructuras discretas, enrutamiento exacto, memoria inmutable y evolución aditiva, capaz de resolver el aprendizaje continuo sin reentrenamiento, sin matrices de pesos y sin riesgo de alucinaciones.

title: From cloud optical thickness to solar radiation: deep spatiotemporal forecasting with geostationary satellite imagery
abstract: Abstract. Accurate short-term cloud forecasting is essential for solar radiation and solar energy applications, where rapidly evolving cloud fields introduce substantial variability in surface solar irradiance. In this study, we develop a hybrid ConvLSTM-UNet deep learning model for 15-min-ahead forecasting of cloud optical thickness (COT) from Meteosat/SEVIRI observations over Europe. The model combines multiscale spatial feature extraction with recurrent spatiotemporal learning and employs a combined Charbonnier–SSIM loss to improve both numerical accuracy and the preservation of cloud structures. The proposed forecasting model is evaluated against real COT satellite retrievals and benchmarked against persistence and a dense optical flow cloud motion vector (CMV) approach. For 15-min-ahead forecasts, ConvLSTM-UNet achieves lower COT prediction errors and higher perceptual quality than both benchmarks, with MAE and RMSE of 1.25 and 9.52, respectively, and SSIM of 0.95. The impact of COT forecast errors on solar radiation is further assessed through the cloud modification factor (CMF), for which the proposed model achieves a forecast skill of approximately 30 % relative to persistence. Its performance advantage is particularly evident under cloudy and rapidly evolving conditions, and remains evident under recursive forecasts extending to approximately 165 min ahead. These results demonstrate the potential of deep spatiotemporal learning for satellite-based short-term cloud and solar radiation forecasting.

title: Assessing Customer Trust in AI-Driven Marketing
abstract: The inception of Industry 4.0 has prompted commercial banks to undergo a transformational shift towards the commercialization of algorithms. This research aims to examine the effects of AI-driven marketing strategies on customer behaviour by focusing on the customer experience and trust, which represent key constructs, based on relationship marketing theory and the Technology Acceptance Model. Data is collected from 200 respondents using standardized questionnaire. The suggested relationships between AI-driven marketing strategies and customer experience and trust were verified with PLS-SEM, and the results indicated that AI-driven marketing has the potential to benefit both customer trust and customer experience. Furthermore, the results show that customer trust serves as an important relational bridge partially mediating the relationship between AI-driven marketing strategies and customer experience.
